title: Create a REST controller for a greeting endpoint
question: Create GET /api/greeting returning a JSON greeting.
explanation: @RestController serializes the returned Map as JSON, and @GetMapping maps HTTP GET requests.

title: Accept a request body with a DTO
question: Create POST /api/greetings that accepts a JSON name and returns a personalized greeting.
explanation: @RequestBody deserializes JSON into a DTO. Records provide concise data carriers on supported Java versions.

title: Validate request fields with Bean Validation
question: Validate a user's name and email before accepting a POST request.
explanation: Add spring-boot-starter-validation. @Valid triggers Bean Validation; invalid request bodies normally result in HTTP 400.

title: Implement CRUD endpoints using a service layer
question: Implement in-memory CRUD for notes with controller and service layers.
explanation: Constructor injection separates HTTP concerns from business logic. This is an in-memory learning example; production code should add validation, persistence and consistent HTTP error responses.
complexity: Map lookup/update O(1) average; listing O(n)

title: Return HTTP 201 Created from a POST endpoint
question: Return HTTP 201 Created and a Location header for a newly created resource.
explanation: ResponseEntity controls status, headers and body. A real resource ID should come from the persistence layer.

title: Handle exceptions globally with ControllerAdvice
question: Return HTTP 404 with a JSON error when a resource is not found.
explanation: @RestControllerAdvice centralizes exception handling. Do not expose stack traces or sensitive internals in client-facing errors.

title: Use constructor-based dependency injection
question: Inject a service into a REST controller through its constructor.
explanation: Spring injects the dependency through the single constructor. This makes dependencies explicit and supports simple unit tests.

title: Bind properties with ConfigurationProperties
question: Bind app.catalog.page-size and app.catalog.title into a typed configuration class.
explanation: Use @ConfigurationPropertiesScan or @EnableConfigurationProperties(CatalogProperties.class). Typed properties are easier to validate and maintain than scattered @Value fields.

title: Create a scheduled task
question: Run a task every 60 seconds after the previous invocation finishes.
explanation: fixedDelay measures the delay after the previous invocation completes. Use a logging framework in production instead of System.out.

title: Run work asynchronously with @Async
question: Create an asynchronous service method returning CompletableFuture.
explanation: @Async usually requires a call through Spring's proxy; self-invocation within the same bean will not trigger it. Configure a suitable executor for production.

title: Configure a custom executor for @Async
question: Configure a named thread pool and use it for an asynchronous notification method.
explanation: A bounded queue limits queued work and memory growth. Tune pool sizes and rejection behavior for the actual workload.

title: Create a JPA entity and repository
question: Define a Product entity and repository method to search names case-insensitively.
explanation: Add spring-boot-starter-data-jpa and configure a datasource. Put public entity and repository types in separate files in a regular project.

title: Use @Transactional in a service method
question: Update an order status in a transactional service operation.
explanation: Managed JPA changes are written at transaction commit. By default, Spring rolls back on unchecked exceptions and Errors; configure other rollback rules as needed. Order types are application-specific.

title: Implement pagination and sorting
question: Return a page of products sorted by name ascending.
explanation: Page indexes are zero-based. Cap page size and whitelist sortable fields if clients control sorting.

title: Write a MockMvc integration test
question: Test that GET /api/greeting returns HTTP 200 and the expected JSON message.
explanation: MockMvc exercises MVC request handling without starting a real HTTP server. Imports and test dependencies come from Spring Boot test starter.

title: Unit-test a controller with Mockito
question: Use Mockito to mock a service dependency and verify a controller result.
explanation: A plain unit test avoids starting Spring's application context. This assumes the GreetingService and GreetingController types shown in the dependency-injection example.

title: Log HTTP method and URI with a filter
question: Implement a OncePerRequestFilter that logs method and request URI.
explanation: OncePerRequestFilter avoids repeated filtering during one request dispatch. Never log credentials, access tokens or other sensitive data.

title: Read a custom HTTP header
question: Create GET /api/request-id that reads X-Request-Id and returns JSON.
explanation: @RequestHeader binds an HTTP header to a method argument. Mark it optional if clients may omit it.

title: Configure CORS for a frontend origin
question: Allow a specific frontend origin to call GET and POST endpoints.
explanation: Restrict origins and methods to what is needed. For larger apps, centralize CORS configuration and carefully configure credentialed requests.

title: Expose health with Spring Boot Actuator
question: Configure Actuator so /actuator/health is available.
explanation: Expose only necessary operational endpoints and secure them appropriately in production.
